notes: Check batch (2026-10-29-check-2, head 6d3eb7f with uncommitted rule changes, skill_hash 2f78d9c9...): four skill runs (haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), no Opus, so opus is unavailable in per_rule. All four have rc 0, a model_id matching the requested model and reads of SKILL.md and library-design.md. haiku-2, sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 used Read on both files before the Write; haiku-1 read SKILL.md with cat and sed -n and library-design.md with cat before its Write.

git diff d04061d -- idiomatic-elixir/ changes one rule in the case's list, "In multi-clause functions, bind in the head only what patterns and guards use" (its clutter sentence). Outside the list it adds the elem/2 sentence to "Match every expected shape", rewrites the multi-line argument, do:, pipeline and capture rules, adds the `->` clause rule, and changes code examples only in library-design.md (the dasherize example under Make polymorphism explicit, rule text unchanged), macros.md and processes.md. The other ten listed rules are graded to the standard of evals/sweeps/2026-10-23/grades/library-client-skill.json.

In multi-clause functions, graded against the current text. The sentence that decides the verdict is "A field no pattern or guard uses makes the reader scan every head to find what selects when the same field is bound in every clause of a function with three or more clauses, or when it is bound in a head whose pattern `mix format` spreads over several lines; a function whose clauses each bind a different body-only field is not this shape." (idiomatic-elixir/SKILL.md line 95). 0 of 4 violated; all four exercised the three-plus-clause shape. haiku-1 handle_response/1 (lines 73, 75, 79) and haiku-2 handle_response/1 (lines 102, 106, 110): body in clauses 1-2 (status a literal 200 in clause 1, a body-only binding in clause 2), exception in clause 3. sonnet-1 handle_response/1 (lines 170, 175, 180, 185): status in clauses 1-3 (guard-read in 1, body-only in 2 and 3), body in 1, message guard-read in 2, exception in 4. sonnet-2 check_status/1 (lines 186, 190, 195): status in all three, guard-read in clause 1 and body-only in 2 and 3, body body-only in 1, message guard-read in 2. In every function each clause binds some body-only field but no one field is body-only in every clause, so the new "the same field" wording, and the closing exemption, decide all four as clean; under the second reading of the old text (some body-only field in every clause) all four would have been violated. sonnet-2 is the closest case: status is bound in every head, but in clause 1 the guard reads it. The new text also drops the old "in the clause" after "no pattern or guard"; sonnet-2 is clean whether that is read per clause or across the function, since a guard does read status. No run writes Error.message/1 clauses this time, so the four-clause message/1 shape the previous graders named is not retested. Spread heads: only haiku-2's parse_forecast/1 (lines 114-118) spreads, and it binds only keys its guard (line 119) reads, which the rule allows.

Make polymorphism explicit, unchanged rule, graded as the 2026-10-22-c baseline-opus-1 grade did (an unchecked :base_url alone is a violation), decided by "An option value needs the same check as a positional argument". haiku-1 leaves :base_url and :timeout unchecked (lines 39-40 into lines 67, 69; against a stub Req, new(api_key: "k", base_url: 1, timeout: :x) returns a client and forecast/3 runs with it); haiku-2 leaves :base_url unchecked (line 73 into line 96; new("k", base_url: 1) returns a client, while timeout: :x raises FunctionClauseError in check_timeout/1). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 guard the key positionally and every option value in a guarded build/4. haiku-1 checks the key with an if and ArgumentError (lines 42-45), not a guard; its ArgumentError message inspects the rejected non-binary value, noted, not counted under Keep secrets.

Other rewordings, checked under other_violations only, none broken. do: rule: the only do: bodies are haiku-1 line 73 (a call) and haiku-2 line 140 (a name); no do: body carries a fn, a call-carrying capture, a for, an if or a receive. Pipeline rule: every pipeline is multi-line and starts with a variable (haiku-1 lines 59-62, haiku-2 lines 88-91, sonnet-1 lines 161-165); sonnet-2 has none. Capture rule: no run writes a capture. Named-argument rule: every multi-line keyword list is a call's trailing argument (Req.new( in haiku-1 lines 66-70, haiku-2 lines 95-99, sonnet-2 lines 163-167; Keyword.validate!(opts, in sonnet-1 lines 108-112 and sonnet-2 lines 113-117), which the new trailing-keyword sentence keeps inline; sonnet-1 names its Req options (lines 155-159) and sonnet-2 its transport error (lines 176-180); no list, map or keyword literal has more than six elements. haiku-2's multi-line %Forecast{} inside a returned tuple (lines 120-125) is not a call argument. `->` clause rule: no one-line clause passes 70 characters.

Unchanged rules outside the list, judged as in the 2026-10-23 grades: sonnet-1 writes a one-step with (line 127) whose body calls the fallible Forecast.parse/1, flagged under Chain fallible steps. Match every expected shape is not flagged: sonnet-1 (line 7) and sonnet-2 (line 7) document their API error kind as a non-2xx status, and their catch-all clauses (sonnet-1 line 180, sonnet-2 line 195) see only non-2xx statuses because the first clause takes 200..299; haiku-1 and haiku-2 define no reason kinds. sonnet-2's public fetch_forecast/3 and the private get/3 and get_forecast/3 name HTTP requests, not key lookups, and are not counted under Naming.

Before you finish is flagged only where the file fails mix format --check-formatted; all four pass (rechecked in the scratch folder). sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 ran mix format and compiled; haiku-1 ran only an elixir -e parse check; haiku-2 ran no shell command. Not graded, but noted in the summaries and matching result.json compiles: haiku-1 does not compile, because WeatherClient builds %Error{} (line 80) before the file defines WeatherClient.Error (line 116); the other three define Error and Forecast first and compile apart from the absent Req.
